segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.

shut the gates of the city against him.
And he gathered an army of Hagarenes and began to fight against it.
And the city came into great distress from the battle and from famine.
And in it a single measure (qfīzā) of salt came to cost four hundred white royal [coins],
and wheat seventy.
And when the common people of the city could not endure the famine and the confinement,
they leapt forth on one of the nights,
and opened the gates of the city,
and brought in Bahādur and the Hagarenes who were with him.
And on that very night he sent heralds up to the minarets of the mosques,
and proclaimed peace to the Muslims and to the Christians,
and encouraged them not to fear,
because his judgment was against the nobles,
and not against the citizens.
And on the morning of the day, he seized the servant of Rukn al-Dīn and imprisoned him.
And Shihāb 'Āriḍ he made ride upon a small donkey,
and led him around the city, and mocked him,
and then killed him.
And another man whose name was Mu'īn Ighdīsh (or: Īgish?) Bāshī,
he tied one end of a cord around his neck,
and the other end around the neck of a dog,
and led him around the city,
and killed him.
And a Greek priest whose name was Kaloyan (Kalojoannes),
and his two brothers, Basil and Manuel,
and his son Kyriori (Kyrios Georgios?),
who were great jurists (nomikoi),
he likewise killed.
And with them also,
the three sons of Shihāb Īsaw,
the Kurdish emirs,
they destroyed {OCR? or: he destroyed}.
Then the slaughter ceased,
and the city was somewhat pacified.
However, the famine grew even more severe after the gates of the city were opened,
because the country was entirely devastated,
and nothing was coming in from another place on account of the Turkmen brigands.
And many were selling their sons and their daughters to the Hagarenes,
and others were soaking old shoes and boiling and eating [them].
And a woman was found who had roasted her son,
and when they judged her,
she swore that she had not killed him,
but after he died, she had roasted him.
And again women were found,
before whom lay the corpse of a dead woman,
and they were cutting pieces from her flesh and roasting and eating [them].
